findings.reason: a node implementing §6 exactly as written would turn five declared-clean files red and be fenced out of repairing them, the same defect §6's sibling §3 and §4 avoid by naming the existing tests that must keep passing.
findings.text: §6's done-when has three cases, all about the `close` verb and the `set` refusal, and states nothing about the existing suite; but refusing `set status` to any value in `TERMINAL_STATUSES` breaks the landing write that at least five test files use as their subject: `tests/test_terminal_status_needs_every_section_ticked.py` (`LAND = {"op": "set", "path": "status", "value": "done"}`), `tests/test_every_section_has_a_declaration.py:278` (asserts the refusal names `s2` and `declaration`, which the new `close` refusal pre-empts), `tests/test_closure_gates.py:128,192,209` (drives `_store.apply_ops` with `set status done` to reach the outcome-gate guard), and `tests/test_continuation.py:102,184,216,265,402` — none of these paths appear in §6's write paths, which list only the new `tests/test_a_plan_closes_in_one_op.py`

findings.reason: an unmeasured clause of the deliverable is one a node can skip and still close on a green gate, which is what the done-when exists to prevent.
findings.text: the deliverable's third clause, that the resolved-placeholder recipe is dropped from `coordinator-reference.md`, `sprint-orchestration.md` and `AGENTS.md`, has no case in the done-when and no grep in its evidence, so a node could leave every `done — no followup` instruction in place and still pass all three cases

findings.reason: the caller left behind keeps instructing a write §6 has just made refuse, and adding the file to the write paths is what makes the "every caller" claim true.
findings.text: §6 states that after the change "every reckon caller that sets one moves to `close` in the same node", but `skills/reckon-create/SKILL.md:609` tells the author to set `plan-status` on the transition to `shipped` ("authored on lifecycle transitions (draft → active → shipped)") and that file is in no §6 write path, so the claim holds only for the two references and `AGENTS.md` it names

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `TERMINAL_STATUSES` resolves at `reckon/lifecycle.py:9`, `_require_transition_verdict` at `reckon/_store.py:3463`, `_refuse_appended_hiding_followups` at `reckon/_store.py:3290`, and the resolved-placeholder recipe resolves in all three files §6 now names (`coordinator-reference.md:1012,1024,1139`, `sprint-orchestration.md:548`, `AGENTS.md:266,295`).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §6's done-when names only the new test file, while the `set status` refusal it introduces breaks at least five existing test files that exercise that exact write, none of them named and none in its write paths.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §6 writes no gate log of its own to a temporary path; its evidence is the pytest artifact and the node's own gate log under the run directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §6 introduces `close` and `tests/test_a_plan_closes_in_one_op.py`, both named by behaviour; the only numbered identifiers are existing symbols it cites.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the deliverable's claim that "every reckon caller that sets one moves to `close` in the same node" is unsupported: `skills/reckon-create/SKILL.md:609` instructs authoring `plan-status` on the transition to `shipped`, and that file is named nowhere in §6.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §6's parts (the `close` verb, the `set` terminal path it replaces, the doc updates that follow) all serve the one stated goal, a plan closing in one write.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s6 depends-on s5 resolves, s6 is declared implementable with no open decision scoped to it (the `deferred-continuation` row now carries `data-sections="s8"`), and the s7←s6 and s8←s7 edges resolve.
